groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word(s) closest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

As the final whistle blew, Amir sat alone on the bench. He had missed the winning penalty during the inter-class football match. He felt __(16: a deep sense of embarrassment)__ as he watched his teammates pack up quietly. His best friend, Kai, noticed that he was deep in thought. Not wanting to __(17: catch him off guard)__, Kai walked over quietly with two bottles of water and spoke in a calm tone, wanting to __(18: allay)__ Amir's worries. "We're not blaming you," Kai said. "Everyone makes mistakes. What matters is that we learn from them." Amir was __(19: deeply)__ touched by Kai's empathy and realised that true friends __(20: stand by)__ one another during difficult times. Their friendship stood the test of time and helped restored Amir's confidence.

Study the texts and then answer questions 21 to 25.

++Text 2++
The extract below is taken from an online article.
School bags are designed to be both roomy and trendy, which makes them appealing to students. Lately, more focus has been placed on making school bags look good. For many students, their school bag is also a way to express their personality and personal style. Is that true for you, too?
While it may seem exciting to fit everything into one bag, have you considered the weight? Carrying too many items strains your back. This may cause short-term discomfort and lead to long-term posture problems. To cushion the effect, you should carry a school bag that fits comfortably on your back. Features such as wide straps and padded backs help distribute the weight more evenly. By choosing a school bag wisely, you can reduce the pressure on your back.
Ultimately, health experts recommend packing only the items needed for the day to keep your school bag light. For example, store certain items in your school locker or keep some materials under your desk if your school allows it. By planning what you bring each day and leaving out unnecessary items, you can protect your back and still have everything you need.

images.alt: Poster. Title: Peaks School Bag. Carry Everything in Style! Say goodbye to boring school bags! Fit your entire school day into one bag, all your books, stationery, lunch boxes and more! Get organised with a specific space for everything! No more mess or things left behind! A picture of a backpack in the middle. On its left: Suitable for students of all ages! On its right: Wide range of colours to choose from! Below: Designed with you in mind! At the bottom, a picture of a smiling boy with the quote: "I love my Peaks school bag! Everything I need for school fits comfortably into it. I can also find and take out any item I need easily!" – Ansel, 12-year-old student

groups.text:
There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
**EACH WORD CAN BE USED ONLY ONCE.**
[[table1]]

Book-sharing corners are becoming a common sight in neighbourhoods across Singapore. More neighbourhoods __(26)__ introduced book-sharing corners where residents can exchange books easily.
__(27)__ traditional libraries, these corners are less structured and have fewer rules. They do not need membership cards and borrowing records, __(28)__ have fixed return dates for borrowed books. In fact, __(29)__ corner has its own selection of books, depending on what residents donate. Readers can take a book home or leave __(30)__ behind for another reader. They are also able to read the books __(31)__ their own pace and not rush to make a return. They may also donate books they no longer need, keeping the collection varied __(32)__ time.
The project is more __(33)__ just a way to reduce waste. It is a simple idea __(34)__ brings neighbours together through reading. __(35)__ talking about the stories they have enjoyed, they get to know one another a little better. In this way, the book-sharing corner helps to build a warmer and more connected neighbourhood.
Adapted from The Straits Times

Each of the underlined words contains either a spelling or grammatical error. Write the correct word in each of the box.

Last month, Hibiscus Primary School organised a Screen-Free Week to help students spend less time on their devices and interact more with others.
Teachers planned several __(36: steemulating)__ activities that not only encouraged students to interact with classmates __(37: and)__ also helped them discover new hobbies. Moreover, setting __(38: away)__ time during recess to play or talk with their peers had forged stronger friendships. By the end of the week, many had become __(39: fermilier)__ with spending their free time away from their devices and had become less __(40: relyant)__ on them.
The principal noted that many students had gained confidence __(41: by)__ the activities and discussions held during the event, __(42: learnt)__ to identify new ways to spend their free time and developing greater __(43: curious)__ about trying new pastimes.
Many teachers regarded the event as a significant __(44: akomplishment)__ because it helped pupils develop greater __(45: ristraynt)__ when managing their screen time. The event encouraged students to make wise choices about their use of devices and to spend their time more meaningfully.
Adapted from The Little Red Dot

Fill in each blank with a suitable word.

The OneMillionTrees movement was launched in Singapore in 2020. With the __(46)__ of planting one million more trees across the island by 2030, this movement reinforces Singapore's long-term __(47)__ to becoming a City in Nature. Parks, nature reserves and park connectors are common __(48)__ where trees are planted to increase greenery across the island. By planting __(49)__ trees, Singapore hopes to create a greener and more sustainable environment for __(50)__ generations.
Trees play many important roles in the environment. They absorb carbon dioxide which helps to regulate temperatures and improve air __(51)__. Their branches and leaves also __(52)__ food and shelter for wildlife. In addition, trees allow animals to __(53)__ freely between parks and nature reserves. As a result, both wildlife and __(54)__ benefit from a healthier environment.
The success of the movement depends greatly on community participation. Members of the __(55)__ can contribute by taking part in educational programmes that teach proper tree care. Some schools even set up small nurseries where young __(56)__ are carefully grown before being planted in gardens. Through these hands-on activities, students gain practical __(57)__ in caring for plants and protecting the environment. As they watch the trees __(58)__ and attract different kinds of wildlife, they develop a __(59)__ appreciation of nature and understand why conserving green spaces is __(60)__.
By working together, Singaporeans can help create a greener and more liveable city for everyone.
Adapted from OneMillionTrees Movement, National Parks Board (NParks)

Refer to the passage below when you answer questions 66 to 75 in Booklet B.

**1** The kindergarten classroom hummed with excitement as children streamed towards the various play corners. With lightning speed, Farid and Lina hurried to their favourite play corner. They took out plastic plates, toy fried eggs and miniature pancakes, and scattered them across a low table.
**2** As usual, Lina handed Farid a tiny apron. With a grin, he took a bow and put on the apron. Then, he pretended to be the chef by raising his hands as if he were putting on a tall chef's hat. Lina appreciated Farid's kindness. Not many children wanted to play with someone who had hearing difficulties. Soon, the pair were immersed in their make-believe café. Farid arranged the eggs neatly onto the pancakes while Lina closed her eyes and pretended to sniff the aroma of the food.
**3** Caught up **in the moment**, Lina reached blindly for a pancake. Her elbow clipped a tray, sending the toy food tumbling onto the floor behind her with a loud clatter. Unaware, she reached again but found only an empty space. Farid let out a short laugh before realising that Lina was tearing up and her shoulders were stiffening.
**4** Leaning closer, Farid gently tapped her shoulder and motioned for her to turn around. As she gasped softly, he made a deliberate scooping motion with his hands. Lina's gaze followed his **movement** and her expression softened. Her fingers brushed against the scattered toy food on the floor. Nodding quickly, she crouched down to retrieve the toy food while Farid helped gather the remaining pieces. Just then, the teacher called for Farid and he left Lina to play on her own.
**5** Moments later, a new wave of activity swept across the classroom. The teacher announced, "Clean up! Time for snack break!"
**6** Chairs scraped against the floor as children hurried to return toys to their shelves. Yet Lina remained seated, oblivious to **the sudden disruption** behind her. She was enjoying her time pretending to feed a cartoon character on the wall poster in front of her.
**7** A child rushing past accidentally knocked against the table, causing several plates to wobble dangerously. Lina glanced about uneasily, her brows furrowing as she looked across the room. Why was everyone moving so quickly?
**8** Sensing that something was amiss, Farid's eyes swept across the room before settling on Lina. Understanding dawned on him as he realised what she had missed. He moved beside her and lightly tapped her shoulder again. As Lina looked up, he glanced at the children tidying the classroom. Then, slowly and carefully, he swept his hands together and pointed towards the toy basket.
**9** Lina studied his face and hands. **Realisation flickered across her features**, and her tense shoulders relaxed. Farid waved to a few classmates, who came over to help. A grateful smile spread across Lina's face. As the children gathered the toy plates and placed them into the basket, Lina followed suit. Together, they finished tidying the play corner.
**10** When they joined the line with their classmates, Lina caught Farid's eye and pressed her hand gently against her chest before extending it towards him. Farid nodded and returned her gesture. Neither of them spoke. Yet in that quiet moment, **Lina's grateful smile and Farid's quiet nod said more than words could.**
Adapted from "This kindergarten put children with and without hearing loss together", CNA Insider, 14 January 2024.

questions.stem: My grandfather had trouble __________ an attachment to his email until I taught him.

explanation: Rule: after the phrase 'have trouble' (and 'have difficulty', 'have a hard time'), the next verb takes the -ing form.
We say 'had trouble adding', just like 'had trouble sleeping' or 'had difficulty walking'.
'to add' is tempting because many verbs are followed by 'to', but 'trouble' is not one of them. 'having added' would mean the adding was already finished, which does not fit.
'My grandfather had trouble adding an attachment...' The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Minah apologised __________ arriving late for the family dinner of her best friend.

explanation: Rule: some verbs always go with the same preposition. We apologise **to** a person **for** something we did.
The thing Minah did wrong was 'arriving late', so the preposition is 'for': 'apologised for arriving late'.
'about' is tempting because we say 'sorry about', but with the verb 'apologise' the correct word is 'for'.
The answer is option (3), for.

questions.stem: The lifeguards continued searching for the missing swimmer in the sea __________ night had already fallen.

explanation: Work out how the two halves are linked. Night falling makes a search harder, yet the lifeguards carried on. The second half is a surprise, a contrast.
'though' (like 'although') joins two ideas that contrast: they continued **though** night had fallen.
'since' and 'because' give a reason, but darkness is not a reason to keep searching. 'unless' gives a condition (if not), which does not fit a past event that had already happened.
The answer is option (3), though.

questions.stem: There was very __________ evidence to support the claim, so the police continued their investigations.

explanation: Rule: 'evidence' is an uncountable noun (we cannot say 'two evidences'). Uncountable nouns take 'little' or 'much'. Countable nouns take 'few' or 'several'.
That rules out 'few' and 'several'. The verb 'was' (singular) is another clue that the noun is uncountable.

Now use the meaning. The police **continued** investigating, so they did not have enough evidence yet. 'very little evidence' means almost none. 'very much evidence' would mean they had plenty, and it is also not natural English in a positive sentence.
The answer is option (2), little.

questions.stem: Everyone on the debate team has submitted the speech outline, __________?

explanation: Rule: a positive statement takes a negative tag, and the tag repeats the helping verb of the statement.
The helping verb is 'has' in 'has submitted' (present perfect), so the tag must use have/has. That rules out 'don't', 'didn't' and 'hadn't' (past perfect).
Special rule: 'everyone' takes a singular verb in the statement ('has'), but in the tag we use the pronoun 'they', and 'they' needs 'have'. So the tag is 'haven't they'.
'Everyone ... has submitted the speech outline, haven't they?' The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: If Ahmad had checked the noticeboard, he __________ where to go for his Art class.

explanation: The 'if' part uses 'had checked' (past perfect). This is about something in the past that did **not** happen: Ahmad did not check the noticeboard.
Rule (third conditional): If + had + past participle, ... would have + past participle.
So the result part is 'would have known'. 'would know' is tempting, but it belongs with 'If Ahmad checked...' (second conditional).
'If Ahmad had checked the noticeboard, he would have known where to go.' The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: The description of the suspect by the witness was consistent __________ the evidence collected by the police.

explanation: Rule: some adjectives always go with the same preposition. 'consistent' goes with 'with'.
'consistent with' means agreeing with or matching. The witness's description matched the evidence.
'to' is tempting because we say 'similar to', but we say 'consistent with', just like 'agree with'.
The answer is option (3), with.

questions.stem: Currently, neither the twins nor their younger brother __________ willing to participate in the competition.

explanation: Rule: with 'neither ... nor ...', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it.
The nearest subject is 'their younger brother', which is one person, so the verb is singular. That rules out 'are' and 'were'.
'Currently' means now, so we need the present tense: 'is', not 'was'.
'are' is tempting because of 'the twins', but the twins are the subject further from the verb. The answer is option (1), is.

questions.stem: The workers __________ the beach since morning, so there is hardly any litter on the ground.

explanation: Clues: 'since morning' tells us the action started in the past and has gone on up to now. 'there **is** hardly any litter' shows the result is in the present.
Rule: for an action that began in the past and has continued over a period up to now, use the present perfect continuous: have/has + been + verb-ing.
'had been cleaning' is the past perfect continuous; it needs another past event to come before, but the result here is in the present ('is'). 'cleaned' (simple past) cannot be used with 'since'.
'have cleaned' is tempting, but with 'since morning' the stress is on the activity going on all that time, so 'have been cleaning' is the best answer. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: The restaurant __________ chefs create award-winning desserts is often very crowded.

explanation: Look at the word after the blank: 'chefs'. The chefs belong to the restaurant (the restaurant's chefs).
Rule: 'whose' shows belonging, and it is followed by a noun. It can be used for things as well as people.
'which' is tempting because a restaurant is a thing, but 'which chefs create' does not make sense: 'which' would have to be the subject or object of 'create', and 'chefs' already is the subject.
'The restaurant whose chefs create award-winning desserts...' The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Despite the heavy downpour, the volunteers remained __________ in their efforts to distribute supplies to the needy.

explanation: Clue: 'Despite the heavy downpour' tells us the volunteers did not give up. We need a word for people who stay firm and determined.
'steadfast' means firm and not changing in what you do or believe. 'remained steadfast in their efforts' is a common phrase.

'unfaltering' is tempting because it has almost the same meaning, but it normally describes a thing (unfaltering support, unfaltering courage), not a person 'in' their efforts. 'immovable' is for something that cannot be physically moved or a person who refuses to change their opinion. 'hesitant' is the opposite idea.
The answer is option (2), steadfast.

review.note: Options (2) steadfast and (3) unfaltering are close in meaning. 'remained steadfast in their efforts' is the standard collocation, and the key agrees.

questions.stem: Jane smiled warmly and nodded __________ as her new classmate shared on her difficulty in making friends in class.

explanation: Clues: Jane 'smiled warmly', and her classmate was sharing a problem. Jane was being kind.
'reassuringly' means in a way that makes someone feel less worried. A warm smile and a reassuring nod go together.
'casually' means in a relaxed way without much care, which does not show kindness. 'reluctantly' (unwillingly) and 'impatiently' do not match a warm smile.
The answer is option (4), reassuringly.

questions.stem: Although his teammates encouraged him, Ryan continued to __________ his own abilities before the competition.

explanation: Clue: 'Although' signals a contrast. His teammates encouraged him, yet Ryan still did not feel confident.
To 'question' your abilities means to doubt them, to be unsure whether you are good enough.

'dismiss' is tempting, but to dismiss something is to decide it is not worth thinking about; we do not usually 'dismiss our abilities'. 'prove' and 'accept' are positive, so they do not contrast with being encouraged.
The answer is option (4), question.

questions.stem: Clear instructions on medicine labels ensure correct __________ of medicine.

explanation: The instructions on a medicine label tell you how much to take and when. We need a word for the giving or taking of medicine.
'administration' of medicine means the act of giving medicine to someone in the right amount and way. (To 'administer' medicine is to give it.)
'supervision' means watching over someone, and 'organisation' means arranging things neatly; labels are not about those. 'digestion' is how the body breaks down food.
The answer is option (4), administration.

questions.stem: Even though the task was not easy, Lily did not __________ from the challenge.

explanation: Look at the word after the blank: 'from'. The phrasal verb must fit with 'from the challenge'.
'back down from' something means to give in or withdraw because it is too hard or frightening. Lily did **not** back down, so she faced the challenge.

'give up' is tempting because the meaning is close, but we say 'give up the challenge' or 'give up on', not 'give up from'. 'pull back' is usually about moving away or troops retreating, and 'turn off' means to switch off.
The answer is option (1), back down.

questions.stem: Choose the word(s) closest in meaning to ++a deep sense of embarrassment++.

explanation: Amir 'felt a deep sense of embarrassment' because he had missed the winning penalty in front of his teammates.
To feel deeply embarrassed about something you did is to feel 'ashamed'.

'awkward' is tempting, but it is a much milder feeling of being uncomfortable; it does not match 'deep'. 'frustrated' means annoyed at not being able to do something, and 'disappointed' means sad that things did not turn out well. Neither is about embarrassment.
The answer is option (1), ashamed.

review.note: The key's digit for Q16 is under the watermark; it shows as a white 1 on the black watermark at zoom and matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word(s) closest in meaning to ++catch him off guard++.

explanation: To 'catch someone off guard' is to surprise them when they are not ready.
Clue: Amir 'was deep in thought', so someone appearing suddenly would give him a shock. That is why Kai 'walked over quietly' and 'spoke in a calm tone'.

'startle' means to give someone a sudden surprise or shock, which matches. 'distract him' is tempting because Amir was thinking, but being caught off guard is about surprise, not about losing attention.
The answer is option (2), startle him.

questions.stem: Choose the word(s) closest in meaning to ++allay++.

explanation: To 'allay' worries or fears is to make them less strong.
Kai spoke calmly and told Amir nobody blamed him. He was trying to make Amir's worries smaller.

'ease' means to make something less painful or serious, and we say 'ease someone's worries'. 'pacify' and 'soothe' are tempting, but we pacify or soothe a **person** (or a baby), not worries. 'resolve' means to solve completely, which is more than 'allay'.
The answer is option (1), ease.

questions.stem: Choose the word(s) closest in meaning to ++deeply++.

explanation: 'deeply touched' means Amir's feelings were moved in a strong and sincere way by Kai's kindness.
'genuinely' means truly and sincerely. 'genuinely touched' keeps the same meaning.
'seriously' is tempting because it can mean 'very', but it is used for bad or grave things (seriously hurt, seriously ill), not for warm feelings. 'fairly' means only quite, which is too weak.
The answer is option (4), genuinely.

questions.stem: Choose the word(s) closest in meaning to ++stand by++.

explanation: To 'stand by' someone is to stay loyal to them and help them when things are hard.
Clue: 'true friends stand by one another during difficult times'. Kai stayed with Amir and comforted him.

'support' means to help and encourage someone, which matches. 'defend' and 'protect' are tempting, but they mean keeping someone safe from an attack, and nobody was attacking Amir. 'motivate' means to make someone want to do something.
The answer is option (3), support.

questions.stem: The slogan "Carry Everything in Style" suggests that the Peaks school bag is both __________.

explanation: Break the slogan into two halves and match each half to one word.
'Carry Everything' tells us the bag does its job well: it holds all you need. That is 'useful'.
'in Style' tells us the bag looks good. That is 'fashionable'.
'large and expensive' is tempting because a bag that carries everything is large, but nothing in the slogan is about price. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Why was Ansel featured in Text 1?
options: He appears to be a good student.
Most school bag users are around his age.
His comments support the claims of the poster.
His review was short enough to fit into the poster.

explanation: Ansel's words are a testimonial: a real user saying good things about a product. Advertisers use testimonials to make their claims more believable.

Compare his words with the poster. Poster: 'Fit your entire school day into one bag'. Ansel: 'Everything I need for school fits comfortably into it.' Poster: 'a specific space for everything'. Ansel: 'I can also find and take out any item I need easily!'
His comments repeat and back up what the poster claims. Option (2) is tempting, but the poster says the bag is 'Suitable for students of all ages', so his age is not the reason.
The answer is option (3).

questions.stem:
Based on Text 1, which of the following statements are true about the Peaks school bag?
A: The bag comes in different colours.
B: The bag helps students organise their belongings
C: The bag is designed to reduce pressure on students' backs.

explanation: Check each statement against the poster (Text 1) only.
A is true: 'Wide range of colours to choose from!'
B is true: 'Get organised with a specific space for everything! No more mess or things left behind!'
C is not in Text 1. Reducing pressure on the back is mentioned only in Text 2, and it is about school bags in general. The question says 'Based on Text 1'. The answer is option (1), A and B.

questions.stem: What is the main focus of Text 2?
options: Choose a school bag that looks attractive.
Avoid carrying too many unnecessary items.
Keep all school materials in lockers or under desks.
Buy a school bag with wide straps and padded backs.

explanation: The main focus is the idea that most of the text builds up to, not a small detail.

Paragraph 2 warns that 'Carrying too many items strains your back.' The last paragraph begins with 'Ultimately' (the most important point): 'health experts recommend packing only the items needed for the day' and 'leaving out unnecessary items'.
Option (4) is tempting, but wide straps and padded backs are only one way to 'cushion the effect'. Option (3) says 'all' materials, but the text says 'certain items' and 'some materials'.
The answer is option (2).

review.note: The key's digit for Q24 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a 2, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Text 1 and Text 2 express differing views on whether __________.
options: school bags should look appealing to students
school bags can fit all books needed for school
students should fit everything into their school bags
students can keep their belongings in school lockers

explanation: Look for a point where the two texts say opposite things.
Text 1 encourages it: 'Fit your entire school day into one bag, all your books, stationery, lunch boxes and more!'
Text 2 warns against it: 'While it may seem exciting to fit everything into one bag, have you considered the weight?' and recommends 'packing only the items needed for the day'.
Option (1) is not a disagreement: both texts accept that bags look good. Option (2) is about whether bags **can** fit the books, which Text 2 does not deny. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the blank is 'introduced', a past participle. We need a helping verb in front of it.
The subject 'More neighbourhoods' is plural, and the first sentence is in the present ('are becoming'), so we use the present perfect: have + introduced.
'had' (E) is tempting, but the past perfect is for something that happened before another past event, and there is no other past event here.
The answer is (F) have.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The sentence compares book-sharing corners with traditional libraries and shows a difference: the corners are 'less structured and have fewer rules'.
'Unlike' means 'different from' and is followed by a noun: Unlike traditional libraries, these corners ...
The answer is (Q) unlike.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The sentence lists things the corners do **not** do: 'They do not need membership cards and borrowing records, ___ have fixed return dates'.
Rule: after a negative ('do not'), we join another thing that is also not true with 'or', not 'and'.
'They do not need membership cards ..., or have fixed return dates' means they do not have fixed return dates either.
The answer is (J) or.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: Look at the words after the blank: 'corner has its own selection'. 'corner' is singular and the verb 'has' is singular.
'each' is used before a singular noun to talk about every one separately, and it goes well with 'its own'.
'all' and 'both' need a plural noun (all corners have). 'one' (H) is tempting, but the sentence is about every corner, not just one of them.
The answer is (D) each.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'Readers can take a book home or leave ___ behind for another reader.' The blank stands for 'a book'.
The pronoun 'one' replaces 'a' + singular noun, so we do not have to repeat 'a book'.
The answer is (H) one.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: '___ their own pace' is a fixed phrase.
We say 'at your own pace', meaning as fast or as slowly as you like. 'at' is used with speeds and rates (at high speed, at a slow pace).
The answer is (B) at.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'keeping the collection varied ___ time'. We need a word that goes with 'time' to mean 'as time passes'.
'over time' is a fixed phrase meaning gradually, during a long period.
'through' (P) is tempting, but 'through time' is not the usual phrase, and 'through' is needed for blank (35).
The answer is (K) over.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: Look at the word before the blank: 'more'. A comparison with 'more' is completed by 'than'.
'more than just a way to reduce waste' means it is that and something extra as well.
The answer is (L) than.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'It is a simple idea ___ brings neighbours together'. The blank joins 'a simple idea' to more information about it and is the subject of 'brings'.
For a thing, the relative pronoun is 'that' (or 'which'). Only 'that' is in the list.
The answer is (M) that.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: '___ talking about the stories they have enjoyed, they get to know one another'. The first part tells us **how** they get to know one another.
'Through' + verb-ing means 'by means of': Through talking about the stories, they get to know one another.
'then' (N) is tempting at the start of a sentence, but 'Then talking about the stories, they get to know...' is not a proper sentence.
The answer is (P) through.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++steemulating++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means making you interested and excited.
Say it in syllables: stim-u-lat-ing. The first sound is a short 'i' (as in 'still'), spelt with 'i', not 'ee'.
It comes from 'stimulate': drop the 'e' and add '-ing'.
The correct word is 'stimulating'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++and++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look earlier in the sentence: 'activities that **not only** encouraged students to interact ...'.
Rule: 'not only' is always paired with 'but also': not only A but also B.
The word 'also' is already there, so 'and' must be changed to 'but'.
The correct word is 'but'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++away++.

explanation: This is a grammar (wrong word) error in a phrasal verb.
To 'set aside' time means to keep some time for a special purpose. Here, time during recess was kept for playing or talking with friends.
'set away' is not an English phrasal verb. Do not confuse it with 'put away' (to tidy something into its place).
The correct word is 'aside'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++fermilier++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means used to something, knowing it well.
Say it in syllables: fa-mil-iar. It is related to 'family', so it starts with 'fam'.
The ending is '-iar' (as in 'peculiar'), not '-ier'.
The correct word is 'familiar'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++relyant++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. 'reliant on' means depending on.
It comes from 'rely'. Rule: when a word ends in a consonant + 'y', change the 'y' to 'i' before adding an ending: rely → reliant, reliable, relies.
The correct word is 'reliant'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++by++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong preposition.
We **gain** something **from** an experience: 'gained confidence from the activities and discussions'. 'through' (by means of) is also correct.
'by' is used for the doer in a passive sentence (was written by him), which is not the case here.
The correct word is 'from' ('through' is also accepted).

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++learnt++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Read to the end of the sentence: '..., ___ to identify new ways ... **and developing** greater curiosity'.
'and' joins two matching forms. 'developing' is not underlined, so it is correct, and the word before 'and' must match it: an -ing word.
The two -ing phrases describe how the students gained confidence: 'learning to identify new ways ... and developing greater curiosity'.
The correct word is 'learning'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++curious++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong word form.
'greater' is an adjective, so it must be followed by a noun: 'developing greater ___ about trying new pastimes'. 'curious' is an adjective.
The noun is 'curiosity'. Watch the spelling: the 'u' in 'curious' is dropped (curi-os-ity).
The correct word is 'curiosity'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++akomplishment++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means something good that has been achieved with effort.
Say it in syllables: ac-com-plish-ment. The 'k' sound is spelt with a double 'c', as in 'accompany' and 'account'.
The correct word is 'accomplishment'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++ristraynt++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. 'restraint' means self-control, holding yourself back.
It comes from the verb 'restrain' (re + strain). It begins with 're', and the long 'a' sound is spelt 'ai'.
Add 't' to make the noun: restrain → restraint.
The correct word is 'restraint'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'With the ___ of planting one million more trees across the island by 2030'. The blank names what the movement wants to achieve.
'with the aim of' + verb-ing is a set phrase meaning 'in order to'.
'goal', 'purpose', 'objective' and 'target' carry the same meaning and are accepted.
The answer is 'aim'.

review.note: 'target' added to accept: 'with the target of planting one million trees by 2030' is clearly correct.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look at the words around the blank: 'Singapore's long-term ___ **to becoming** a City in Nature'.
We need a noun that is followed by 'to' + verb-ing and means a firm promise to keep working at something. That is 'commitment to'.
'long-term commitment' is a common word pair.
The answer is 'commitment'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Parks, nature reserves and park connectors are common ___ where trees are planted'.
'where' tells us the blank is a word for a place. It must be plural to match 'are' and the three examples.
'places', 'locations', 'spaces', 'areas' and 'sites' all fit.
The answer is 'places'.

review.note: 'sites' added to accept: 'common sites where trees are planted' is clearly correct.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look back at the first paragraph: the aim is 'planting one million **more** trees'.
'By planting ___ trees, Singapore hopes to create a greener ... environment'. Greener means adding to the trees already there, so 'more trees'.
The answer is 'more'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'a greener and more sustainable environment for ___ generations'.
'Sustainable' means able to last a long time, so the environment is being protected for people who will live later: 'future generations' is the set phrase.
The answer is 'future'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'They absorb carbon dioxide which helps to regulate temperatures and improve air ___.'
When trees take in carbon dioxide, the air becomes cleaner. How clean the air is, is called 'air quality'. We 'improve' quality.
'pollution' does not fit because we reduce pollution, not improve it.
The answer is 'quality'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Their branches and leaves also ___ food and shelter for wildlife.' We need a verb meaning 'give'.
The subject 'branches and leaves' is plural and the paragraph is in the present tense, so the verb has no 's': 'provide'.
'provide ... for' is a common pattern: provide food and shelter for wildlife. 'offer' also fits.
The answer is 'provide'.

review.note: 'offer' added to accept: 'offer food and shelter for wildlife' is clearly correct.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'trees allow animals to ___ freely between parks and nature reserves'.
After 'allow animals to' we need the base form of a verb. 'between parks and nature reserves' shows the animals go from one place to another.
'move' fits. 'wander', 'travel' and 'roam' mean the same here.
The answer is 'move'.

review.note: 'travel' and 'roam' added to accept: both are clearly correct with 'freely between parks and nature reserves'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'As a result, **both** wildlife **and** ___ benefit from a healthier environment.'
'both ... and ...' joins two groups. The paragraph has talked about animals; cleaner air and cooler temperatures also help people.
The verb 'benefit' has no 's', so the noun is plural: 'humans' or 'people'.
The answer is 'humans'.

review.note: 'people' and 'residents' added to accept: 'both wildlife and people benefit' is clearly correct.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Members of the ___ can contribute by taking part in educational programmes'.
The sentence before talks about 'community participation'. Ordinary people are called 'members of the public'. 'members of the community' also fits.
The answer is 'public'.

review.note: 'community' added to accept: 'members of the community' is clearly correct and echoes 'community participation' in the sentence before.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'small nurseries where young ___ are carefully grown before being planted in gardens'.
A nursery is a place where young plants are grown. The verb 'are' shows the noun is plural.
'plants' fits. 'trees', 'saplings' (young trees) and 'seedlings' also fit.
The answer is 'plants'.

review.note: 'trees', 'saplings' and 'seedlings' added to accept: each is clearly correct for what is grown in a nursery in a tree-planting movement.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Through these hands-on activities, students gain practical ___ in caring for plants'.
'hands-on' means learning by doing. What you get from doing something yourself is 'practical experience'. We 'gain experience in' doing something.
'skills' and 'knowledge' also go with 'gain practical ... in'.
The answer is 'experience'.

review.note: 'skills' and 'knowledge' added to accept: 'gain practical skills/knowledge in caring for plants' is clearly correct.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'As they watch the trees ___ and attract different kinds of wildlife'.
Rule: after 'watch' + object, use the base form of the verb (watch the trees grow), and it must match 'attract'.
The trees were planted young, so over time they 'grow'.
The answer is 'grow'.

review.note: 'mature', 'flourish' and 'thrive' added to accept: each is a base-form verb that clearly fits.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'they develop a ___ appreciation of nature'. We need an adjective that goes with 'appreciation'.
After watching the trees grow, the students value nature more than before, so a comparative fits: 'a deeper appreciation' or 'a greater appreciation'.
The answer is 'deeper'.

review.note: 'deep' and 'stronger' added to accept: 'a deep appreciation' and 'a stronger appreciation' are clearly correct.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: '... and understand why conserving green spaces is ___.' We need an adjective after 'is'.
The whole passage shows how useful trees are, so the students see that looking after green spaces matters.
'important' fits. 'necessary', 'crucial', 'essential' and 'vital' mean the same.
The answer is 'important'.

review.note: 'essential' and 'vital' added to accept: both are clearly correct.

questions.stem:
If you charge the battery fully, your phone will not run out of power.
____________________ unless ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Your phone will run out of power unless you charge the battery fully.
accept: Your phone will run out of power unless you charge the battery fully

explanation: 'unless' means 'if ... not'. It already carries a 'not', so one of the two halves must switch between positive and negative.
The given sentence says: charge fully → will **not** run out. With 'unless' in the middle we say what happens if you do not charge it: the phone **will** run out of power.
Keep the 'unless' part positive: 'unless you charge the battery fully'. Do not write 'unless you do not charge'.
Answer: Your phone will run out of power unless you charge the battery fully.

review.keyAnswer: Your phone will run out of power unless you charge the battery fully.
review.solvedAnswer: Your phone will run out of power unless you charge the battery fully.

questions.stem:
The match was cancelled as the weather was bad.
Owing to ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Owing to the bad weather, the match was cancelled.
accept: Owing to the bad weather the match was cancelled.
Owing to bad weather, the match was cancelled.

explanation: 'Owing to' means 'because of'. It is a preposition, so it must be followed by a noun phrase, not a clause with a verb.
Change the clause 'the weather was bad' into a noun phrase: 'the bad weather'.
Put a comma after the opening phrase, then write the result in full: 'the match was cancelled'.
Answer: Owing to the bad weather, the match was cancelled.

review.keyAnswer: Owing to the bad weather, the match was cancelled.
review.solvedAnswer: Owing to the bad weather, the match was cancelled.

questions.stem:
He spoke to her politely although he was upset.
____________________ in spite of ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: He spoke to her politely in spite of being upset.
accept: He spoke to her politely in spite of the fact that he was upset.
He spoke to her politely in spite of his being upset.
He spoke to her politely in spite of feeling upset.

explanation: 'in spite of' shows contrast like 'although', but it is a preposition. It must be followed by a noun or a verb-ing, not by a subject and verb.
Change 'he was upset' to the -ing form: 'being upset'. Drop 'he was'.
Keep the order of the given sentence because 'in spite of' is in the middle: He spoke to her politely in spite of ...
Another correct way is to add 'the fact that' and keep the clause: 'in spite of the fact that he was upset'. Answer: He spoke to her politely in spite of being upset.

review.keyAnswer: He spoke to her politely in spite of being upset. Accept: He spoke to her politely in spite of the fact that he was upset.
review.solvedAnswer: He spoke to her politely in spite of being upset.

questions.stem:
"How do you plan to get home after the party?" Uncle Joe asked his daughter.
Uncle Joe asked his daughter how ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Uncle Joe asked his daughter how she planned to get home after the party.
accept: Uncle Joe asked his daughter how she planned to get home after the party

explanation: In reported speech a question becomes a statement: the subject comes before the verb, 'do' is dropped, and there is no question mark.
Change the pronoun: 'you' is his daughter, so it becomes 'she'.
Move the tense one step back because the reporting verb 'asked' is in the past: 'do you plan' becomes 'she planned'.
Answer: Uncle Joe asked his daughter how she planned to get home after the party.

review.keyAnswer: Uncle Joe asked his daughter how she planned to get home after the party.
review.solvedAnswer: Uncle Joe asked his daughter how she planned to get home after the party.

questions.stem:
Tim was able to complete the task because his sister encouraged him.
With ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: With his sister's encouragement, Tim was able to complete the task.
accept: With the encouragement of his sister, Tim was able to complete the task.
With his sister's encouragement Tim was able to complete the task.
With encouragement from his sister, Tim was able to complete the task.

explanation: 'With' is a preposition, so it must be followed by a noun phrase, not a clause.
Change the verb 'encouraged' into its noun form, 'encouragement', and show whose it is: 'his sister's encouragement' (remember the apostrophe).
Put a comma after the opening phrase. Then name the person in the main clause: 'Tim', not 'he', because Tim has not been mentioned yet.
Answer: With his sister's encouragement, Tim was able to complete the task.

review.keyAnswer: With his sister's encouragement, Tim was able to complete the task. Accept: With the encouragement of his sister, Tim was able to complete the task.
review.solvedAnswer: With his sister's encouragement, Tim was able to complete the task.

questions.stem: In paragraph one, why did Farid and Lina hurry to their favourite play corner with lightning speed?

answer.value: They were excited to play at their favourite play corner.

explanation: Paragraph 1 opens with the mood in the room: 'The kindergarten classroom hummed with excitement as children streamed towards the various play corners.'
Farid and Lina were part of that excitement, and the corner was their 'favourite', so they could not wait to play there.
The marker looks for the feeling (excited / eager) and what it was about (playing at their favourite play corner).

review.keyAnswer: They were excited to play at their favourite play corner.
review.solvedAnswer: They were excited / eager to play at their favourite corner. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Why did Farid take a bow after Lina handed him the apron?

answer.value: He wanted to thank Lina for handing him the apron.

explanation: Find the sentence in paragraph 2: 'As usual, Lina handed Farid a tiny apron. With a grin, he took a bow and put on the apron.'
The bow comes straight after he receives the apron, and he is grinning, so it is a friendly way of saying 'thank you'.
He used an action instead of words because Lina had hearing difficulties (stated later in the paragraph).
The marker looks for: to thank Lina / to show his appreciation for the apron.

review.keyAnswer: He wanted to thank Lina for handing him the apron.
review.solvedAnswer: To thank Lina (using a gesture, as she could not hear well). Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Why did Farid pretend to put on a chef's top hat instead of telling Lina he was the chef?

answer.value: Farid knew that Lina had hearing difficulties, so he gestured to help her understand that he was pretending to be the chef.

explanation: The reason is given a little later in paragraph 2: 'Not many children wanted to play with someone who had hearing difficulties.' The 'someone' is Lina.
Point 1 (1 mark): Lina had hearing difficulties, so she might not hear him if he spoke.
Point 2 (1 mark): by acting it out ('raising his hands as if he were putting on a tall chef's hat'), he helped her understand that he was the chef.
A 2-mark 'why' question needs both the cause (her hearing difficulties) and what the action achieved (she could understand him).

review.keyAnswer: Farid knew that Lina had hearing difficulties, so he gestured to help her understand that he was pretending to be the chef.
review.solvedAnswer: Lina had hearing difficulties and would not hear him, so he used actions she could see and understand. Agrees with key.
review.note: The question says "chef's top hat" while the passage says "tall chef's hat"; transcribed as printed.

questions.stem: Based on lines 11 to 14 (paragraph 3), provide two pieces of evidence that suggest that Lina was upset when the food tumbled onto the floor.

parts.label: i
explanation: Look at the last sentence of paragraph 3: Farid realised 'that Lina was tearing up and her shoulders were stiffening'.
'tearing up' means her eyes were filling with tears, which shows she was upset.
Write it as a full sentence about Lina: Lina teared up / Lina was tearing up. The two pieces of evidence can be given in either order.

parts.label: ii
explanation: The same sentence gives a second sign: 'her shoulders were stiffening'.
When a person is upset or tense, the body goes stiff.
Do not use 'Farid let out a short laugh'; that is about Farid, not evidence of Lina's feelings.

review.keyAnswer: (i) Lina teared up. (ii) Lina's shoulders stiffened.
review.solvedAnswer: She was tearing up; her shoulders were stiffening. Agrees with key.

questions.stem:
Based on the given information, fill in the following table.
(For each situation, write Lina's feeling, then the three-word phrase from the passage that shows it.)

parts.label: ai
parts.prompt:
Situation (a): When Lina realised that she had dropped the toy food on the floor (paragraph 4).
Lina's feeling:
explanation: In paragraph 4, Farid tapped Lina's shoulder and made her turn around. That was the moment she saw the toy food on the floor.
The passage says 'she gasped softly'. A gasp is a sudden breath we take when we are shocked or surprised.
Accepted feelings: shocked / surprised / startled. 'Relieved' is wrong here; her expression softened only afterwards, when Farid showed her how to scoop the food up.

parts.label: aii
parts.prompt:
Situation (a): When Lina realised that she had dropped the toy food on the floor (paragraph 4).
Three-word phrase from the passage:
explanation: Find the words in paragraph 4 that show shock: 'As she gasped softly, he made a deliberate scooping motion with his hands.'
Count exactly three words and copy them without changing anything: she (1) gasped (2) softly (3).
The answer is 'she gasped softly'.

parts.label: bi
parts.prompt:
Situation (b): When Lina saw everyone moving quickly (paragraph 7).
Lina's feeling:
explanation: In paragraph 7, Lina 'looked across the room' and the writer gives her thought: 'Why was everyone moving so quickly?'
A question like that shows she did not understand what was going on, so she was confused (puzzled).
The feeling must match the phrase you choose in the next blank.

parts.label: bii
parts.prompt:
Situation (b): When Lina saw everyone moving quickly (paragraph 7).
Three-word phrase from the passage:
explanation: Find the words in paragraph 7 that show confusion: 'Lina glanced about uneasily, **her brows furrowing** as she looked across the room.'
To furrow your brows is to frown so that lines appear on your forehead, which people do when they are puzzled.
Count exactly three words: her (1) brows (2) furrowing (3). The answer is 'her brows furrowing'.

review.keyAnswer: (a) Shocked — "she gasped softly" (b) Confused — "her brows furrowing"
review.solvedAnswer: (a) shocked / surprised — "she gasped softly"; (b) confused / uneasy — "her brows furrowing" (or "glanced about uneasily"). Agrees with key.
review.note: The answer booklet gives 4 marks for four cells, taken as 1 mark per cell. For (b), the pairing Uneasy — "glanced about uneasily" is also a three-word phrase from paragraph 7 that a teacher may accept; the key lists only Confused — "her brows furrowing", so only that phrase is auto-marked as correct.

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the words or phrases in the left column refer to in the passage? Write your answers in the column on the right.

parts.label: a
explanation: For a 'refers to' question, read the sentence just before the word.
Sentence before: 'he made a deliberate scooping motion with his hands.' Then: 'Lina's gaze followed **his movement**'.
'his movement' is that scooping motion. Say whose it was: Farid's scooping motion with his hands.

parts.label: b

answer.value: The children tidying up / hurrying to return the toys to their shelves

explanation: Read the sentence just before the phrase: 'Chairs scraped against the floor as children hurried to return toys to their shelves.'
That noisy rush of activity is 'the sudden disruption behind her' which Lina did not notice.
The marker looks for: the children tidying up / returning the toys to their shelves.

review.keyAnswer: (a) "movement" — Farid's scooping motion (b) "the sudden disruption" — the children tidying up / returning the toys to their shelves
review.solvedAnswer: (a) Farid's deliberate scooping motion with his hands; (b) the children hurrying to return toys to their shelves. Agrees with key.

questions.stem:
Read the statement below.
**Lina wanted to finish feeding the cartoon character before tidying up the toys.**
Do you agree with the statement? Yes / No (Tick one box only)
Support your answer with evidence from the passage, excluding Lina's hearing disability.
(Write Yes or No, then give two pieces of evidence, (i) and (ii).)

answer.value:
No.
(i) Lina could not see what the other children were doing because her back was turned.
(ii) Lina did not realise that tidy-up time had begun.

explanation: The statement says Lina **chose** to carry on playing. Check whether she even knew it was time to tidy up.
Evidence (i): the tidying was happening 'behind her', and she was facing 'the wall poster in front of her', so she could not see the other children returning the toys.
Evidence (ii): she was 'oblivious to the sudden disruption' and later wondered, 'Why was everyone moving so quickly?' She did not realise that tidy-up time had begun.
So the answer is No: she did not carry on because she wanted to finish first; she simply did not know. Do not use her hearing difficulty as evidence, because the question excludes it.

review.keyAnswer: No. (i) Lina could not see what the other children were doing because her back was turned. (ii) Lina did not realise that tidy-up time had begun.
review.solvedAnswer: No. The clean-up was behind her while she faced the wall poster, so she did not see it; she was oblivious and later wondered why everyone was moving so quickly, so she did not know it was time to tidy up. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: What does the phrase **"Realisation flickered across her features"** (line 34, paragraph 9) tell you about Lina's understanding at that moment?

answer.value: Lina suddenly understood what Farid was trying to tell her and realised that it was time to tidy up.

explanation: 'Realisation' means suddenly understanding something. 'flickered across her features' means it showed quickly on her face, like a light coming on.

Point 1 (1 mark): at that moment Lina suddenly understood what Farid was telling her with his hands. Just before this, he 'swept his hands together and pointed towards the toy basket', and she 'studied his face and hands'.
Point 2 (1 mark): say what she understood: it was time to tidy up. Evidence that follows: 'her tense shoulders relaxed' and she 'followed suit'.
Answer with both: she suddenly understood Farid's gestures and realised it was time to tidy up.

review.keyAnswer: Lina suddenly understood what Farid was trying to tell her and realised that it was time to tidy up.
review.solvedAnswer: She had just (suddenly) understood from Farid's gestures that it was time to tidy up. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: At the end of the passage, Lina pressed her hand against her chest before extending it towards Farid. What did this gesture show? Why?

answer.value: The gesture showed that Lina was thankful to Farid. She wanted to thank him for helping her understand that it was time to tidy up.

explanation: There are two questions, so give two parts: what the gesture showed (1 mark) and why (1 mark).

What: a hand on the heart, then held out to someone, is a way of saying 'thank you' without words. The passage calls it 'Lina's grateful smile', and earlier 'A grateful smile spread across Lina's face.' So it showed she was thankful (grateful) to Farid.
Why: Farid had noticed what she had missed and used gestures to help her understand that it was time to tidy up (he also called classmates over to help).
Answer: it showed Lina was thankful to Farid, because he had helped her understand that it was time to tidy up.

review.keyAnswer: The gesture showed that Lina was thankful to Farid. She wanted to thank him for helping her understand that it was time to tidy up.
review.solvedAnswer: It showed her gratitude to Farid, because he had helped her understand it was time to tidy up. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: What does the writer mean by "Lina's grateful smile and Farid's quiet nod said more than words ever could" (lines 40 – 41, paragraph 10)?

answer.value: Lina and Farid understood each other without needing to speak.

explanation: The sentence before says 'Neither of them spoke.' So the smile and the nod were doing the talking.
Point 1: they did not need to speak. Lina's smile told Farid she was thankful, and his nod told her he understood.
Point 2: 'more than words ever could' means these actions showed their feelings and their friendship more strongly than talking would have.
Answer: Lina and Farid understood each other (her thanks and his acceptance) without needing to speak.

review.keyAnswer: Lina and Farid understood each other without needing to speak.
review.solvedAnswer: They understood each other's feelings (her gratitude, his acceptance) through gestures alone, without speaking. Agrees with key.
review.note: The question quotes "said more than words ever could"; the passage prints "said more than words could". Both transcribed as printed.
